A wicketkeeper-batsman who struck the ball as cleanly and as hard as anyone of his generation, with a brief, happy taste of Test cricket along the way.

Where it began

Heinrich Klaasen was born in Pretoria on 30 July 1991 and went to school at Hoërskool Menlopark. He learned his trade in the domestic game with the Titans and Northerns.

Even as a young player he caught the eye of Shukri Conrad, then a coach at the national academy, who compared his calm under pressure with that of MS Dhoni. It was a bold thing to say about a youngster, and Klaasen spent the following years proving him right.

The player

White-ball cricket came first. He was called into South Africa's one-day side against India in February 2018 and won a match award in only his second game. Before the month was out he had a Twenty20 international fifty too, and on 29 February 2020 he made his first one-day hundred, an unbeaten 123 against Australia.

His Test debut followed against India on 19 October 2019. He played 4 Tests between 2019 and 2023, making 104 runs with a best of 35 and taking 10 catches and 2 stumpings behind the stumps. In 2021 he also had the honour of leading South Africa in Twenty20 internationals.

What made him special

Klaasen's gift was clean, fearless hitting. At the 2023 World Cup he made 109 against England in Mumbai. In the 2024 T20 World Cup final he raced to fifty faster than anyone had in the final of a global tournament, and his 52 off 27 balls nearly carried South Africa home.

The leagues loved him. He made 110 from 44 balls for the Seattle Orcas, the first hundred in Major League Cricket, and in the 2025 IPL he reached three figures off just 37 balls on his way to 105 not out. Test cricket saw only a glimpse of him, four matches in all, but the shorter game was very glad to have the rest.

Away from the middle

His cricket took him around the world: Rajasthan Royals, Royal Challengers Bangalore and Sunrisers Hyderabad in India, Durban's Super Giants at home, and stops in North America. He announced the end of his international career in June 2025 and afterwards carried on in the franchise leagues, where bowlers had long since learned to fear his name on the team sheet.

And finally

Twice he was picked for brand-new tournaments that were called off before a ball was bowled, one of them in Glasgow. Scottish rooftops may never know how lucky they were. And that first one-day hundred, made on 29 February, means he gets a proper anniversary only once every four years.
